{{Short description|2009 mathematics textbook by Loring W. Tu}}
{{Italic title}}
'''''An Introduction to Manifolds''''' is a mathematics textbook written by [[Loring W. Tu]] providing an introduction to differential and integral calculus on [[smooth manifold]]s.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Tu |first1=Loring W. |date=2011 |title=An Introduction to Manifolds |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4419-7400-6 |series=Universitext |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4419-7400-6 |isbn=978-1-4419-7399-3}}</ref> It was first published in 2008 by [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] and received positive reviews.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Berg |first=Michael |date=April 19, 2008 |title=An Introduction to Manifolds |url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/an-introduction-to-manifolds |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=MAA Reviews |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cap |first1=A. |title=Book Reviews |journal=Monatshefte für Mathematik |date=September 25, 2010 |volume=161 |issue=3 |page=354 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00605-010-0237-5 |publisher=SpringerLink |doi=10.1007/s00605-010-0237-5 |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The book is meant as a precursor to ''Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology '' by [[Raoul Bott]] and Tu.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Feldman |first=D. V. |date=June 2008 |title=An Introduction to Manifolds |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/225728177 |journal=Choice: Current Reviews for Academic Libraries |volume=45 |issue=10 |pages=1807 |doi=10.5860/CHOICE.45-5637 |doi-broken-date=19 September 2025 |id={{ProQuest|225728177}} }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Bott |first1=Raoul |last2=Tu |first2=Loring W. |title=Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4757-3951-0 |series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics |publisher=Springer |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4757-3951-0 |date=1982 |volume=82 |isbn=978-1-4419-2815-3 }}</ref>
